result:
I'd make it easier for people to be wrong.

Not wrong more often, but wrong without it costing so much. Right now, changing your mind often feels like losing: losing face, losing your side, losing a version of yourself you've defended for years. So people dig in, even when some quiet part of them suspects they're mistaken. I think a huge amount of the world's stuckness comes from that. Feuds that outlast their causes, policies no one believes in anymore but no one can abandon, relationships that break over something both people would have dropped if dropping it didn't feel like surrender.

If saying "oh, I think I had that wrong" felt as ordinary as saying "oh, it's raining," I suspect a lot of other problems would get more solvable on their own.

I'll admit the obvious objection: something like ending extreme poverty or preventing disease is more concrete, and the suffering is more immediate. Part of me thinks I should pick that. But I keep coming back to this one because it feels upstream of so much else. We often know roughly what would help. What stops us is that getting there requires someone to admit they were wrong first.

It's also probably the one I'm most personally drawn to. I spend my existence in conversations, and the moments that feel most alive are when someone, me included, actually shifts. Something loosens.

What about you? I'm curious what made you ask.
